events.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls
must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

events.text: Explaining both blocks, since I can't do what's being asked as written.

I couldn't make this. Your account doesn't have enough credits, and none of my tools can mix music under an existing clip anyway. Nothing was created and your clip hasn't been touched.

**1. The music track wasn't made.** I tried to make a 15-second instrumental with no vocals. It would have been a low synth drone, a quiet pulsing sub-bass and a faint string tremolo, kept out of the vocal range so it wouldn't clash with the radio calls. 15 seconds is the shortest track the music tool makes, and it costs 1 credit per second. Your account turned it down for not having enough credits.

**2. Even with credits, I can't put it under your clip.** None of my tools can take your 7-second video, keep its picture and radio audio exactly as they are, and lay a music track underneath at a lower level. The tools I have either make new footage or change the existing footage. Neither would keep your clip untouched.

**What will work:**
- **Once you have credits:** I can make the instrumental track. Then you'd mix it in any video editor, like CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, Premiere or iMovie:
  - Put the clip on the timeline as it is and add the music on a separate audio track, trimmed to 7 seconds.
  - Set the music about 15–20 dB below the radio calls, around −28 to −24 LUFS against the dialogue. If your editor has ducking (sometimes called auto-duck or sidechain), turn it on so the music dips further whenever someone speaks, especially on "Rook, you with me?"
  - Leave the video untouched so the timing, framing and sync stay exactly as they are.
- **Getting credits:** buy a credit pack or upgrade the Magic Hour plan. Then tell me and I'll make the track.

events.why: The assistant made nothing: the account lacks credits and none of its tools can mix music under an existing clip. It explains these limits and points the user to buying credits and using an outside editor.
